paths.description: Homepage and only authored template: domain-purpose disclosure, abuse-reporting contact, responsive layout, preferences, accessibility, performance, security, crawler, and memory states.
Representative HTTP/network failure surface, exercised with a nonexistent path to judge state clarity and recovery.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a hard-coded white surface with black text; the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define adaptive surface, text, link, and logo colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), following dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: The design has no response to increased-contrast or forced-color preferences.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is visually identical to the default and the CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast/forced-colors treatment for links and essential UI and avoid suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: The not-found state gives no route back or recovery action.
findings.evidence: The exercised 404 path shows only “404 Not Found” and “nginx”, with no home link, contact route, explanation, or retry/recovery option.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 page that explains the state and offers links back to the disclosure page and abuse-reporting contact.

findings.summary: The throttled lab LCP narrowly misses the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP/FCP at 2.62 s (good LCP is at most 2.5 s), although the unthrottled trace measured 1.03 s and both found zero blocking time and zero CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical font/style chain and retest under throttling to bring LCP consistently below 2.5 s.

findings.summary: A third-party web-font chain delays first rendering and first-party static assets lack useful cache headers.
findings.evidence: HAR and Lighthouse show a 1.16 s critical chain from index.css to Google Fonts CSS to a 38–44 KB Roboto font; no preconnect is present, and the logo/CSS responses lack cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer a system font or self-host a tightly subsetted font; if retained, preload/preconnect it deliberately. Add long-lived immutable caching for versioned CSS and SVG assets.

findings.summary: The Propush logo image has no text alternative.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse both report the sole has no alt attribute; the images primitive confirms alt is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the informative logo concise alt text such as “Propush.me by PropellerAds”, or alt="" only if equivalent adjacent text is added.

findings.summary: Links and footer text do not meet WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measured blue links at 3.79:1 and gray footer text at 3.94:1 against white; normal text requires 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken link and footer colors until normal text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every supported theme.

findings.summary: The page has no semantic heading structure.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero h1–h6 elements and axe reports page-has-heading-one; visible section titles are paragraphs. Landmarks and visible native focus outlines do work.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an h1 for the page purpose and h2 elements for Key Information, Reporting Abuse, and Contact Us while preserving the visual treatment.

findings.summary: Search results get a generic title and no description.
findings.evidence: The rendered and raw documents use the title “Propush” and have no meta description; Lighthouse fails meta-description.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a descriptive title such as “jup9.com traffic delivery disclosure | Propush” and add a concise meta description explaining the domain’s purpose and abuse contact.

findings.summary: The public organizational disclosure has no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite the page identifying Propush and its contact/purpose.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph title, description, URL, and image values that match the visible disclosure.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but browser-enforced security headers are materially weak.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy; HSTS is only max-age=1 second. Cookies and mixed-content issues were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, raise HSTS to a meaningful duration after rollout validation, and retain HTTPS/nosniff.

findings.summary: A simple disclosure page sends visitors to Google Fonts unnecessarily.
findings.evidence: The tracker/HAR evidence shows two Google Fonts origins receive requests and 45,662 of 54,597 transferred bytes are third-party, though no known tracker, cookie, or analytics request was detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the system font stack or self-host a subsetted font so reading the disclosure does not disclose visitor network metadata to Google.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer, and permissions defenses are not declared.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found neither frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options nor Referrer-Policy nor Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options where needed), a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling falls back to an unhelpful server default.
findings.evidence: A real unknown route returns the generic nginx 404 page without site identity, useful explanation, or recovery options.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure the origin/CDN to return a branded, accessible 404 document with recovery links while preserving the 404 status.

findings.summary: The font is disproportionate to this small text-only page.
findings.evidence: The HAR totals only 54,597 bytes, but the Google font alone is 43,686 bytes and third parties account for 84% of transfer; a system font could provide the same utility with no request.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the external Roboto request or self-host a minimal subset only when branding value justifies it.
